source: FAO Plant Production and Protection Division — Tomato cultivation (illustrative smallholder guide)
spacing: 45–60 cm between plants, 90 cm between rows; stake or cage for airflow.
how_to_grow: Start seedlings in a nursery bed or trays for 4–6 weeks. Transplant when plants have 4–6 true leaves and night temperatures stay above 15°C. Water at the base in the morning; mulch to retain moisture. Remove suckers on indeterminate varieties if you want fewer, larger fruit.
harvest_signs: Pick when fruit is fully coloured for the variety but still firm. Harvest every 2–3 days in peak season. Do not leave overripe fruit on the plant — it attracts pests and reduces new fruit set.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.watering: Keep seedbed moist but not waterlogged; light watering twice daily in hot weather.
stages.nutrients: No heavy fertilizer in the nursery. A thin layer of well-rotted compost in the transplant hole is enough at this stage.

stages.name: Vegetative
stages.watering: Deep watering 2–3 times per week; increase frequency in sandy soil or dry spells.
stages.nutrients: Side-dress with compost or a balanced NPK (e.g. 10-10-10) about 2 weeks after transplant — follow local extension rates; avoid excess nitrogen late in this stage.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.watering: Consistent moisture is critical; irregular watering causes blossom-end rot and flower drop.
stages.nutrients: Shift toward potassium and phosphorus; reduce nitrogen. Compost tea or a low-nitrogen blend supports flowering and fruit set.

stages.name: Fruiting
stages.watering: Maintain even soil moisture; mulch helps. Reduce watering slightly as fruit ripens to improve flavour.
stages.nutrients: Potassium-rich feeding (e.g. wood ash or K-focused organic mix per local advice) supports fruit size and colour.

stages.name: Harvest
stages.watering: Water only as needed to prevent wilting; avoid overhead irrigation near harvest.
stages.nutrients: Stop heavy feeding 2–3 weeks before final harvest; focus on picking and post-harvest handling.
